status: Research-only integrated case and trace; known outcomes disclosed; no accepted additional lane or axis.

case.starting_question: Does an environmental transcriptional response identify a directly recognized signal, and which regulator-state/target relations actually follow?

actual_observations.observation: Cluster-ligand Cys variants retained activation of sufA/ydiU and repression of hyaA; abundance increased, so stronger effects did not establish stronger per-molecule activity.
Clusterless protein bound hya but not randomized DNA. Selected hya base substitutions impaired both competition and repression while leaving basal promoter output largely intact.
The same target-site class included activation and repression; a sequence-logo T-rich region partly overlapped promoter elements.
actual_observations.source_location: Discussion: Characteristics of a Type 2 site

actual_observations.observation: iscR sites A/B controlled repression, whereas footprinted site C did not under tested conditions. Clusterless variants lost iscR repression despite increased protein abundance.
More total IscR was required for half-maximal repression aerobically. Added FNR demand derepressed iscR aerobically, but not anaerobically.
actual_observations.source_location: Cluster occupancy and demand Results; Figure 7

actual_observations.observation: E43A preserved hya affinity approximately but expanded apo-protein recognition to a type-1 site. Symmetrizing the type-1 dinucleotide alone did not restore wild-type apo binding.
Solved structures used clusterless variants. Relocation of the specificity determinant upon cluster loading was proposed rather than directly observed.
Air-exposed protein assayed anaerobically bound iscR DNA similarly with or without dithionite; authors interpreted oxidation as irrelevant to binding.
PMS weakened type-1 binding in purified preparations without detected iron release anaerobically; apo-protein/type-2 control binding persisted.
Air-exposed protein bound poorly when assayed in air but recovered binding after chamber return. Authors proposed auto-reduction, revising the earlier interpretation.
At controlled IscR expression, anaerobic PMS affected type-1 repression but did not reproduce apo-favored type-2 regulation. Aerobic treatment affected both promoter classes.
OxyR/Fur controls helped attribute reporter changes; superoxide assays and SOD controls separated cluster destruction from the anaerobic PMS effect.

case.annotation_consequence: Supports a cofactor-state-dependent sequence-specific regulator with target-dependent activation/repression. Direct cofactor redox action is distinguishable from indirect assembly-demand feedback; neither implies a demonstrated selective PMS-binding pocket. DNA occupancy alone does not specify productive control or its sign.
case.experiment_dependence: Authors’ promoter and protein mutants, reporter transcription, quantitative protein blots, purified DNA binding, cofactor/iron-release measurements and structural experiments. None were performed here.
case.reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Published outcomes were known. Observations belong to authors; connecting decision problems and comparison with existing lanes are retrospective reconstruction. Historical interpretations are preserved beside their later revision.
case.verification_scope: Five primary papers’ relevant complete paths inspected as itemized in sources. One independent published-table/oligo arithmetic probe was run. No biological experiment, new regulon scan, raw-curve fit or IscR structure computation.
case.count_unit: One regulator/function-allocation question across multiple states, target promoters and papers; not separate cases for target genes, mutants or studies.

iscr_type2_2009.title: Sequence-specific binding to a subset of IscR-regulated promoters does not require IscR Fe-S cluster ligation
iscr_type2_2009.inspection: Complete relevant main Results/Discussion and Methods: Cys variants and abundance, hya binding/random DNA, oligo mutation/competition library, native promoter mutations and target-class comparisons. Published Table 1 sequences/central IC50 values were transcribed for the explicit probe. Supplementary files/raw curves were not reanalyzed.

iscr_cluster_2012.title: Characterization of the [2Fe-2S] cluster of Escherichia coli transcription factor IscR
iscr_cluster_2012.inspection: Complete DNA-binding oxidation-state Results subsection, Figure 9 description, corresponding fluorescence Methods, and relevant cluster characterization/Discussion passages. Spectroscopic raw data and all ligand-mapping experiments were not independently reanalyzed. Its oxidation-independent interpretation is historical and explicitly revisited by the 2025 paper.

iscr_homeostasis_2013.title: Regulation of iron-sulphur cluster homeostasis through transcriptional control of the Isc pathway by [2Fe-2S]-IscR in Escherichia coli
iscr_homeostasis_2013.inspection: Complete main Results and relevant Discussion; promoter-site perturbation, protein abundance, Isc/Suf supply, functional titration and FNR-demand comparisons. Growth, blots, footprinting and anisotropy Methods read. Figure S1 numeric threshold is the main-text report, not a supplementary-data reanalysis.

iscr_specificity_2013.title: Studies of IscR reveal a unique mechanism for metal-dependent regulation of DNA binding specificity
iscr_specificity_2013.inspection: Complete main Results/Discussion and Online Methods: apo/3CA structures, protein and DNA mutations, Tables 2/4, type-1/type-2 discrimination and holo-mechanism limits. No independent IscR coordinate calculation or supplementary curves reanalysis. All solved structures in this study lack the cluster; the proposed holo conformational path is not directly visualized.

iscr_redox_2025.title: The Role of the [2Fe-2S] Cluster of Escherichia coli IscR in Responding to Redox-Cycling Agents
iscr_redox_2025.inspection: Complete main Results, Discussion and relevant Methods: PMS response, OxyR/Fur controls, iron-release/superoxide comparisons, redox-treatment/assay atmosphere, type-1/type-2 reporters at controlled protein expression, and physiological rescue limits. Supplementary document and raw curves not reanalyzed. Intracellular state pools and chamber auto-reduction are source interpretations rather than independently measured here.

starting_alternatives: The environmental variable directly changes IscR.
It changes cofactor supply or total regulator abundance indirectly.
Another regulator creates the measured promoter response.
trace.changed_uncertainty: A reporter can change while the regulator is more abundant yet less competent at one target. The identity of the changed molecular quantity must be resolved.
trace.comparison_reported: Compare cluster-ligand variants across promoter classes, measure protein abundance, perturb assembly machinery and introduce another Fe–S client demand.
trace.why_this_comparison_reconstructed: A deletion/expression change alone merges input sensing, abundance and output control. These contrasts separate loss of all protein function from a state-specific target defect and test a competing indirect input route.
trace.result_boundary: The demand interpretation gained support; it did not prove that every oxygen/PMS response is exclusively indirect or quantify all intracellular cluster-state fractions.

starting_alternatives: A weaker target response reflects general DNA-binding failure.
The protein discriminates a different target set with similar affinity at a reference site.
The promoter mutation changes basal transcription rather than regulator recognition.
trace.comparison_reported: Use randomized competitors, individual DNA substitutions, basal-output controls, protein-side substitutions and a compensating DNA-site change.
trace.why_this_comparison_reconstructed: A structure contact or an unchanged reference-site affinity cannot establish conserved target range. Comparing the candidate discriminator on both DNA classes asks whether the property lost is binding energy or exclusion of other sequences.
trace.revision: The contact-to-affinity shortcut fails: E43 removal leaves hya binding nearly intact while broadening recognition. The unsuccessful site symmetrization also rejects an explanation resting only on that dinucleotide.
trace.result_boundary: The source supports sequence discrimination; a motif scan still cannot supply regulatory sign, promoter productivity or an observed holo conformational trajectory.

starting_alternatives: PMS destroys the cluster, forming apo-IscR.
It changes the cofactor redox state without cluster loss.
It nonspecifically damages DNA/protein or produces the effect only through another cellular component.
trace.comparison_reported: Under defined assay atmospheres compare PMS, air, iron release, clusterless-protein binding and return of air-treated protein to the chamber.
trace.why_this_comparison_reconstructed: The early negative comparison relied on a treatment label standing in for the state present during binding. Replaying the treatment and readout environments tests that assumption before rejecting redox control.
trace.revision: The 2025 result adds a redox-responsive state to the occupancy picture and proposes that assay-environment reduction masked the earlier effect. Auto-reduction is the authors’ interpretation, not an independently measured state trajectory here.
trace.result_boundary: Direct action on an isolated cofactor-bearing preparation supports a molecular input route. It is not a PMS ligand-binding/selectivity experiment, and it does not remove indirect demand feedback from cells.

starting_alternatives: All DNA-bound states produce the same regulatory output.
Cofactor states can bind yet differ in productive activation/repression.
Changing IscR abundance or other promoter regulators explains the output difference.
trace.comparison_reported: Inspect target-site classes, sites with and without measured transcriptional consequences, controlled regulator expression and reporters with other regulatory sites removed.
trace.why_this_comparison_reconstructed: An occupancy experiment asks where the regulator can bind. A signed control relation requires a promoter-output contrast at comparable regulator expression with alternative regulatory inputs addressed.
trace.revision: A footprinted site can lack a detected output effect; the same binding-site class can support opposite signs; oxidation and cluster loss do not reproduce the same target responses.
trace.result_boundary: Target sequence, regulator state and promoter architecture constrain the relation. A generic regulator label or binding motif cannot replace those functional claims.

coverage_assessment.candidate_annotation_question: Which input acts on the regulator, through what molecular or indirect route, and which targets does that state productively activate or repress?
coverage_assessment.provisional_conclusion: This is an explicit regulatory relation worth making visible, but this one integrated case does not establish a sixth lane or independent credit axis. It can currently be investigated through F01 recognition specificity and F03 causal control, provided input recognition and productive target relations are actually examined.
coverage_assessment.F01_connection: DNA-site and input/cofactor recognition are molecular specificity questions. I6 shows that preserved affinity for one reference DNA does not preserve the set of recognized targets.
coverage_assessment.F03_connection: The causal contribution is a relation: changing a regulator state may alter binding, productive transcription, indirect assembly demand or total abundance. I4/I11 show why occupying a site is not the same contribution as controlling its output.
coverage_assessment.why_not_a_data_type_axis: Reporter, binding, structural and cofactor measurements can each support different links in the same proposed relation. The question concerns the claimed function, not whether evidence came from RNA-seq, EMSA, ITC or another assay.
coverage_assessment.why_not_merely_a_condition_label: Ordinary observation context must always be preserved. Here state is also part of the function being assigned because target eligibility and productive activation/repression differ. Recording “aerobic” alone does not establish which state or relation caused the effect.

comparison_with_imported_cases.use: Existing record supports regulatory/promoter involvement without direct maltose-recognition evidence. Not reinspected as a new primary case.

Existing record separates repression from direct 5-OP binding/selectivity. IscR shows that a direct input can instead chemically alter a cofactor; a ligand-binding-pocket test is not universal. Not counted again.

compatibility_limits: The reusable decision is to distinguish response, molecular input and productive target control; their assays are not interchangeable.
PxpR metabolite binding cannot be copied onto IscR redox chemistry, or MalR nutrient dependence onto direct maltose binding.
Partial cluster occupancy, different oligos/salt concentrations, assay atmosphere and promoter architecture prevent pooling the papers’ apparent affinities into one intrinsic specificity ranking.
The apo mutants are experimentally useful proxies; they are not a direct quantitative measurement of every physiological state pool.
The 2013 specificity structures are clusterless. The structural hypothesis for holo-state remodeling remains distinct from its measured binding phenotype.
No regulatory question, tool, evidence measurement or conditional state is adopted as a new scoring axis.
coverage_assessment.central_table_status: F01–F05 and the three-slot table were read. No central table/index was edited, no F06 added, and no implementation changed.

actually_used_here: Read existing comparison/linked case records and exact-word duplicate search.
Retrieve five primary full texts and inspect complete relevant experimental paths.
Align seven published hya oligos and calculate within-source ratios while preserving censored and approximate measurements; script and input provenance are saved.
possible_computational_evidence: Promoter-aware motif discovery/scanning, e.g. MEME/FIMO, with experimental site classes and transcription-start information retained; this can nominate sites rather than determine regulatory sign.
Compare conserved protein recognition residues and deposited interfaces to nominate specificity tests; clusterless coordinates cannot visualize the missing holo transition.
Analyze appropriately matched occupancy/expression time courses if suitable data are supplied; no such dataset or raw-curve availability was assumed here.
author_wet_lab_dependencies: Controlled regulator/cofactor-state preparations and direct chemical input assays.
Native or controlled-expression promoter reporters with DNA-site/alternative-regulator controls.
DNA-competition and affinity experiments, protein abundance measurements, cofactor/iron-release assays, and structure-guided mutagenesis.
not_done: No new motif/genome scan, dataset reprocessing, binding experiment, structural simulation or intracellular-state measurement.
No extra agents, repository edits, implementation/design changes or scoring changes.

duplicate_check.scope: Before new source retrieval, exact-word case-insensitive IscR search across /tmp/episode-published-cases JSON/JSONL/Markdown records returned no match. Earlier broad substring search also returned words such as discrimination and was discarded as a duplicate test.
